skill.name: hyperframes
skill.description: Routes video, motion graphics, captioning, slideshow, website, product, music, and pull request requests to specialized HyperFrames workflows.
skill.summary: Selects the right HyperFrames workflow and directs HTML-based video production.
skill.author: heygen-com

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks around skill names, file names, and workflow labels. The skill does require remote CLI execution and mutable skill updates before workflows, and it describes automatic website crawling with headless Chrome.

remediation.issue: Workflow routing requires remote package execution and skill updates before use.
remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation, pin package and skill versions, verify integrity, and use a preinstalled CLI when possible.

remediation.issue: Product and website workflows may resolve and crawl supplied or inferred URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Ask before browsing, allow only approved public HTTPS hosts, and block private, loopback, link-local, and metadata addresses.

semantic_findings.title: Mandatory Mutable Skill Installation Before Workflow Use
semantic_findings.description: The router requires an npx update before reading a selected workflow and can install missing or stale remote skills. This expands executable instructions without an explicit user approval step or version pin.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file explicitly says to run the update before reading the workflow and states that missing or stale skills are installed or refreshed.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic URL Resolution and Headless Browser Crawling
semantic_findings.description: Product and website workflows resolve or crawl supplied and inferred sites with headless Chrome. Without destination controls, untrusted URLs could expose the browser to hostile content or internal network targets.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The crawling behavior is explicit, but the referenced workflow implementation is unavailable, so existing URL validation controls cannot be verified.

content.value_statement: Choosing the correct video workflow can be difficult. This skill routes each request to a specialized HyperFrames process and provides operational guidance.
actual_capabilities: Routes product promos, website tours, explainers, captions, overlays, music videos, slideshows, migrations, and general video requests.
Maps composition, animation, keyframe, creative, media, CLI, registry, and Figma needs to specialized domain skills.
Selects default aspect ratios from the destination and preserves the user's language for narration and captions.
Distinguishes captioning, talking-head overlays, motion graphics, music-driven video, and full video production.
Provides commands for checking, updating, and installing HyperFrames workflows and core skills.
Documents the expected inputs, outputs, and trigger phrases for each supported workflow.
limitations: The router does not contain the complete implementation for any specialized workflow.
Rendering requires the HyperFrames CLI and related skills to be installed.
Footage retiming, recoloring, reframing, reordering, and audio editing are outside the caption and overlay workflows.
Some workflows browse websites, use GitHub tools, or install skills, which require network and command permissions.

use_cases.title: Create a Product Promo
use_cases.description: Route a product URL, brief, or script into a launch video workflow with suitable defaults.

use_cases.title: Explain a Code Change
use_cases.description: Turn a GitHub pull request into a concise visual release or changelog video.

use_cases.title: Transform Existing Media
use_cases.description: Choose captioning, graphic overlays, music-driven editing, motion graphics, or slideshow production from supplied assets.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Route this request to the best HyperFrames workflow: [request]. State the selected workflow, required input, and important limitation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner routing for a clear request

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Product Video
prompt_templates.prompt: Route and plan a [duration] product video for [product]. Use [destination], [language], and these source materials: [materials].

prompt_templates.title: Transform Existing Footage
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [media description] and choose captions, graphic overlays, music-driven video, or another workflow. Explain why the alternatives do not fit.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Complex Production
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a routing brief for [project]. Cover workflow selection, domain skills, aspect ratio, language, dependencies, approval points, validation, and final deliverables.

output_examples.input: Make a 45-second launch video for our analytics product using its website.
output_examples.output: Selected product-launch-video. The plan uses website assets, a 16:9 frame, a concise value narrative, and an MP4 deliverable.

output_examples.input: Add readable subtitles behind the speaker in this interview clip.
output_examples.output: Selected embedded-captions. The footage remains unchanged while locally generated captions can be occluded by the speaker.

output_examples.input: Convert this presentation outline into an interactive deck with speaker notes.
output_examples.output: Selected slideshow. The deliverable is a navigable deck with slides, reveals, presenter controls, and notes rather than a rendered video.

best_practices: Provide the source material, subject, destination, and desired output before routing.
Confirm network browsing and package updates before running commands or capturing websites.
Use the selected workflow first, then load only the domain skills required for production.
anti_patterns: Do not choose general-video when a specialized workflow clearly matches the request.
Do not treat captioning or graphic overlays as complete nonlinear video editing.
Do not run mutable updates silently or crawl URLs that the user has not approved.

faq.question: Does this skill render videos by itself?
faq.answer: No. It routes requests and relies on HyperFrames workflows, domain skills, and CLI tools for implementation and rendering.

faq.question: Which workflow handles a product website?
faq.answer: Use product-launch-video for a promotional result. Use website-to-video when the goal is a direct site tour.

faq.question: Can it edit existing talking-head footage?
faq.answer: It can route caption and graphic-overlay work. Retiming, recoloring, reframing, reordering, and audio editing remain outside those workflows.

faq.question: Can it create presentations?
faq.answer: Yes. The slideshow workflow produces a navigable deck with slides, fragments, branching, hotspots, presenter mode, and speaker notes.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: Often. Skill updates, website capture, product crawling, and GitHub pull request access can require network connectivity.

faq.question: Should automatic skill updates be allowed?
faq.answer: Review and approve them first. Pin versions and verify sources because updates can change the instructions and code used during production.
